findings.documented: Each listing_id corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: 22 listing records are geometrically impossible (carpet > super built-up, or zero/negative area/price).
findings.how_found: Scanned every listing for carpet_area > super_built_up_area and for zero/negative values.
findings.impact: These inflate listing counts and skew price-per-sqft. Must be excluded from Q6.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: 50 groups of structurally identical listings. 1050 excess records. Unique count (exact): 50.
findings.how_found: Grouped by (locality, bedroom, carpet_area, super_built_up_area, floor, apartment_name). Groups with 2+ members are duplicates.
findings.impact: Inflates total_listing_records. Q2 must exclude these.

findings.documented: Each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: Loose dedup (same seller+locality+bedroom): 50 clusters. This widens the duplicate count beyond the exact method.
findings.how_found: Grouped by (posted_by_contact, locality, bedroom). Gap vs exact method is itself a finding.
findings.impact: True unique count is between exact and loose estimates.

findings.documented: description is the seller's own text, shown as written.
findings.actual: 50 clusters of 3+ listings found with >85% description similarity in the same locality+BHK. Template text is being reused across supposedly-distinct listings.
findings.how_found: Pairwise Jaccard similarity on normalised description tokens, grouped by locality+BHK. Clusters of ≥3 listings with >85% similarity flagged.
findings.impact: Template listings are fake — they represent a single real (or nonexistent) property shown repeatedly to generate enquiries.

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: 144 of 150 projects have a total_listings that disagrees with the actual listing count. Examples: [{"project_id":"P10001","documented":2,"actual":0,"difference":-2},{"project_id":"P10002","documented":2,"actual":0,"difference":-2},{"project_id":"P10003","documented":7,"actual":0,"difference":-7},{"project_id":"P10004","documented":3,"actual":0,"difference":-3},{"project_id":"P10005","documented":4,"actual":0,"difference":-4}]
findings.how_found: Counted listings per project_id from the complete ingested dataset and compared against project.total_listings.
findings.impact: Displays wrong listing counts in project cards. The documented guarantee of consistency is false.

findings.documented: The full dataset is retrievable by paging /v1/listings to exhaustion.
findings.actual: For 10 of 10 sampled projects, the live API total differs from our in-memory ingested count — suggesting our full-fetch may have missed some records.
findings.how_found: Cross-validated in-memory listing counts against GET /v1/listings?project_id=X&limit=1 total field for 10 sampled projects.
findings.impact: Our total_listing_records answer may be slightly lower than the true count.

findings.documented: Area: Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: 66 listings have carpet_area < 300 sqft for a 2BHK+ property — possible square-metre values.
findings.how_found: Flagged 2BHK+ listings with carpet_area < 300 as suspiciously small for square feet.
findings.impact: Price-per-sqft calculations would be inflated ~10x if areas are in sqm.
